speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a young person presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; have you noticed if these lesions appeared before or after you started feeling the fever and pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic arthritis of the left wrist likely caused by *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*.

The history of recent sexual activity, the "migratory" joint pain involving the knee, fever, chills, and localized wrist inflammation after a camping trip strongly suggests disseminated gonococcal infection. I need to confirm this with specific testing. REQUEST TEST: Urine_Nucleic_Acid_Amplification_Test, Blood_Culture, and Synovial_Fluid_Analysis. REQUEST IMAGES: X_Ray_left_wrist.
